nodes.question: What is the concept of peri-urban areas, and why are they considered as zones of transition?
nodes.answer: Peri-urban areas are zones of transition from rural to urban land uses located between urban and regional centres and the rural environment. They are considered zones of transition because urban development extends into rural and industrial land, resulting in porous and transitory boundaries.

nodes.question: Why is the Ile-de-France region significant in terms of size and population?
nodes.answer: The Ile-de-France region is one of the smallest regions in France, covering only 2.2% of the total surface area, yet it accommodates a significant portion of the population, making it a densely populated area by urbanization.
nodes.paragraph: We hypothesised that toads liv - ing in habitats impacted by human land use would differ in morphology. We predict that individuals from urban habi - tats will be larger and show relatively longer limbs allow - ing them to overcome landscape barriers. Animals from more open, agricultural habitats, for example, could be expected to be larger for physiological reasons (desiccation avoidance) as suggested higher. We further predict that the responses of males and females will be different because of the difference in reproductive behaviour with males having longer forelimbs due to their role in amplexus and females having larger bodies due to their investment in eggs. nodes.answer: High-resolution satellite imagery was used, following building-aggregation and road communication criteria.

Woody vegetation in Xalapa is diverse and heterogeneous, with the configuration of the trees and shrubs mainly shaped by the necessities and preferences of citizens and government plans (Falf in and MacGregor-Fors 2016 ). nodes.question: How were the sampling sites for the survey chosen?
nodes.answer: Subgroups of survey sites were randomly selected for urban and reference areas, with line limits drawn above and below each reference site to determine the sampling areas.
nodes.paragraph: In addition to the importance of the reference points as remnants of the original vegetation, those areas allow for the free transit of people, in contrast with some other similar areas in the surroundings of Xalapa that are private property or insecure places non-suitable for surveying. Unfortunately, urban and agricultural sprawl in the Southeast region of the study area makes it almost impossible to survey a similar sampling design for a tropical dry forest representation, restricting the analyses only to the other two types of vegetation in the region. To analyze comparable samples, we randomly selected subgroups for the urban and reference survey sites. Given the location of the reference sites, we drew line limits of 1 min (~ 11.1 km) above and below the location of each reference site. Within those bands, we selected subgroups of nine survey sites each from the available pool that var - ied in amount because of the irregular shape of the urban continuum of Xalapa.
